claim_verdicts.evidence: Definitional: the informal statement that names the principle, identical to outline item 1. Pinned .NET docs only list the name ("- Liskov substitution principle") without a formulation; no official source in versions.yaml defines it, and the lesson adds no specific rule beyond the definition.

git show stage-1:.../Oop/ShippingFee.cs: abstract class ShippingFee { public abstract int ForOrder(int totalVnd); }; StandardShipping => totalVnd >= 2_000_000 ? 0 : 30_000; ExpressShipping => 60_000; PickUpInStore => 0. No throw anywhere, so every int input yields an int. Round 2: section 2 "same shape as ShippingFee, one method ForOrder" also holds: ShippingFee.cs:5-8 and ShippingFeeLspViolation.cs:7-10 each declare only public abstract int ForOrder(int totalVnd).

git show stage-1:.../Design/ShippingFeeLspViolation.cs lines 7-24: ShippingFeeBase { public abstract int ForOrder(int totalVnd); }; StandardShippingOk => totalVnd >= 2_000_000 ? 0 : 30_000; BulkOnlyShipping => totalVnd >= 5_000_000 ? 45_000 : throw new InvalidOperationException("order too small for bulk shipping"). Section 5 block matches lines 7-24 character-for-character.

override.md: "An `override` method must have the same signature as the overridden base method. `override` methods support covariant return types." tips-for-java-developers.md: "C# doesn't have the concept of *checked exceptions*. Any method might (in theory) throw any exception." Covariant returns do not affect this int-returning case.

git show stage-1:.../SamplesTests.cs lines 18-24: var kinds = new ShippingFee[] { new StandardShipping(), new ExpressShipping(), new PickUpInStore() }; Assert.Equal(new[] { 0, 60_000, 0 }, kinds.Select(kind => kind.ForOrder(2_000_000))). Block matches exactly.

Traced from ShippingFeeLspViolation.cs:14,22-23: StandardShippingOk(500_000): 500_000 >= 2_000_000 false -> 30_000; (6_000_000) -> 0. BulkOnlyShipping(6_000_000): >= 5_000_000 -> 45_000; (500_000) -> throw new InvalidOperationException("order too small for bulk shipping").
Line 23 uses `totalVnd >= 5_000_000 ? 45_000 : throw ...`; 5_000_000 satisfies >=, so a test asserting 45_000 at exactly 5,000,000 passes while every total below throws.

cs0534.md: "A class is required to implement all the abstract members in the base class, unless the class is also abstract." abstract.md: "Non-abstract classes that derive from the abstract class must implement members marked as abstract." Round 2 text now carries the non-abstract condition ("in any subclass that is not itself abstract").

Follows directly from the definition in claim 1 applied to the verified behaviour in claim 3 (throws below 5,000,000 where the base declares only int ForOrder(int)); no external fact is asserted. Round 2: opened stage-1 ShippingFee.cs, ShippingFeeLspViolation.cs, SamplesTests.cs, refs cs0534.md/abstract.md/override.md; all round-1 issues resolved; zero issues.

issues.text: The q4 scenario says 'In production' and 'the fee step'. 'Production' is not in my known vocab and the lesson never uses it; 'the fee step' is not a named thing anywhere in the lesson. I can guess the answer anyway, but I stop on both phrases.
issues.quote: In production, the fee step calls `ForOrder` with every order's total, and many orders are below 5,000,000.
issues.fix: Replace with the lesson's own wording: 'In the running system, code that works out a fee for any order calls `ForOrder` with every order's total, and many orders are below 5,000,000.' Same in vi.

issues.text: The new introduction of `ShippingFeeBase` works (round-1 issue resolved), but it is inserted mid-sentence between dashes and I re-read it twice: 'alongside a well-behaved StandardShippingOk' could attach to `ForOrder` or to the base class.
issues.quote: It derives from `ShippingFeeBase` — a second base class in the samples with the same shape as `ShippingFee`, one method `ForOrder`, alongside a well-behaved `StandardShippingOk` — overrides `ForOrder`, and compiles.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: 'It derives from `ShippingFeeBase`, overrides `ForOrder`, and compiles. `ShippingFeeBase` is a second base class in the samples with the same shape as `ShippingFee` (one method, `ForOrder`); its other subtype, `StandardShippingOk`, behaves well.'
